blockers.detail: DG-MAIN's call cockpit (app/ui/CallConsole.tsx, app/api/call-console/route.ts) now captures a real appointment date/time inline when the rep logs a 'Termin' outcome, and writes it straight into the pipeline (sales_opportunities.next_action_at) instead of only logging the outcome text. Peer source was inspected read-only (components/caller-queue.tsx, supabase/migrations/026_call_outcome_rpc.sql): CLIENT-WALKENHORST's energy_record_call_outcome RPC has the same gap today (a 'meeting' outcome only sets lead status + an activity note, no date/time is captured or stored anywhere, no energy_meetings/appointments table exists). This is a new capability, not a divergence from an existing peer feature, and DG-MAIN has no push access to the walkenhorst repo (read-only per AGENTS.md instance isolation). Parity requires a separate reviewed change made directly in CLIENT-WALKENHORST's own repo by whoever operates that instance (e.g. extend energy_record_call_outcome to accept p_meeting_at and persist it), not a push from this session.

Peer's lead-facing video/analysis page was not found to have an equivalent booking-calendar embed either (peer only wires a calendar link, same as DG-MAIN did before this change). New capability, same reasoning and same read-only constraint as caller-queue-inline-appointment-booking-2026-09-28: parity is a separate reviewed change for CLIENT-WALKENHORST's own maintainers.

No Walkenhorst runtime data, credentials, branding or customer logic were copied.

No peer runtime data, credentials, branding or customer-specific logic were read or copied. rules: Never replace the established Pflege UX with a new parallel dashboard to port a shared feature.
Adapt shared behavior into the existing Pflege surface.
Never create a second primary Pflege workspace; /pro must resolve back to the canonical root workspace.
Never lower the Pflege A+ qualification gate merely to fill the daily lead target; expose the deficit and keep searching instead.
Never copy customer data, credentials, Supabase refs, branding or industry-specific logic between instances.
Do not mark a shared-core task complete until both instances are adapted or a blocker is recorded here.
